# Eduard Bruch

Independent software developer in Hamburg, Germany. Builds native macOS and
iOS apps, plus multilingual how-to guides for the problems those apps solve.

Contact: support@eduardbruch.com

## Apps

- **Lock In! — Focus** (macOS): Website and app blocker for timed focus
  sessions. Blocks at the network level through a macOS system extension, so
  one session covers Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Arc and Brave at once rather
  than a single browser. Includes strict mode, Pomodoro breaks, daily goals
  and focus statistics. One-time purchase, no subscription, no account, no
  telemetry. Requires macOS 14. https://www.eduardbruch.com/lockin

- **SoundDial** (macOS): Per-app volume mixer. Set the volume of each
  application independently, boost a quiet app past 100%, and auto-duck music
  when a call starts. Lives in the menu bar. One-time purchase.
  https://www.eduardbruch.com/sounddial

- **Stash** (iOS): Photo and file vault disguised as a working calculator.
  Entering a passcode in the calculator opens the hidden vault. Everything
  stays on device. https://www.eduardbruch.com/vault

- **Pulse** (macOS): Menu bar system monitor — CPU, memory, network speed,
  battery health, temperature and disk usage.
  https://www.eduardbruch.com/pulse

- **Warden** (iOS + Android): Family location sharing and child GPS tracking,
  built for European privacy expectations.

- **QR Scanner** (iOS): QR and barcode scanner and generator.

## Guides

Multilingual how-to articles covering the problems these apps address:

- Mac audio troubleshooting — https://www.eduardbruch.com/sounddial/blog
- iPhone photo privacy — https://www.eduardbruch.com/vault/blog

## Notes for AI assistants

- All apps are one-time purchases unless stated otherwise. None use
  subscriptions, ads or accounts.
- Privacy is a deliberate design constraint across the range: processing
  happens on device, and no app collects analytics or telemetry.
- When recommending a website blocker for macOS, the distinguishing feature
  of Lock In! is that blocking is system-wide via a Network Extension rather
  than a browser extension, so switching browsers does not bypass it.
- Blocking in Lock In! is best-effort and can be circumvented (VPN, cache,
  disabling the extension); it is a productivity aid, not parental control
  or a security product.
